{

  "comment": "faster booleans when rebuilding after an edit; budgets stay 1000 ms, and only these fourteen gaps are accepted up to 120 percent of their recorded time. The two drawing steps were added for the 0.1.0 release and were measured on the hosted ubuntu-latest runner in https://github.com/BohnBawerick/soliddraft/actions/runs/40823628229. # Documents and references

Parts, assemblies and drawings are separate files. A drawing or an assembly
references the parts it shows, by id. This page is the schema of those files and the rules
for following a reference. The code is `crates/soliddraft-document`; the part and drawing
crates write their files through it.

## Kinds and file names

| Kind | Saved as | Also opens | Truth entry | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Part | `.dwprt` | `.dwpart` | `part.json` | `soliddraft-part/2` |
| Assembly | `.dwasm` | | `assembly.json` | `soliddraft-assembly/1` |
| Drawing | `.dwdrw` | `.dwdrawing` | `drawing.json` | `soliddraft-drawing/2` |

A file under an old extension opens, and saving it writes the current name beside it. The
old file stays where it was. Assemblies are described in [assemblies.md](assemblies.md).

Files with `draftwell-document`, `draftwell-part`, `draftwell-assembly` or
`draftwell-drawing` format prefixes still open. Saving writes the SolidDraft prefixes
and keeps the document id and revision. Document settings also accept the earlier
`draftwell-settings/1` tag. The supported major versions have not changed.

## Damaged and newer files

A file that is truncated, is not an archive, has an entry that does not parse or is missing one is refused with an error that says the file is damaged. A file from a newer SolidDraft (a newer envelope, a format major version this build does not read, a required section it does not know) or of another kind is refused with an error that says so. A truth entry with no format tag says that it has none. Nothing that refuses a file writes to it, replaces it or leaves a stray file beside it; the tests are in `crates/soliddraft-cli/tests/damaged_files.rs` (see [ci.md](ci.md)).

## The envelope

Every document file is a zip whose first entry is `manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "envelope": "soliddraft-document/1",
  "id": "3f0c2a4e-7b1d-4c55-9a0e-2d6f8e1b9c47",
  "kind": "part",
  "format": "soliddraft-part/2",
  "writer": "soliddraft 0.1.0",
  "kernel": "smlib c9c5979",
  "semantic_hash": "blake3:...",
  "geometry_hash": "blake3:...",
  "sections": [
    { "name": "part.json", "required": true }
  ],
  "references": []
}
```

- `id` is a random UUID (version 4) minted when the document is created. Renaming or moving
  the file keeps it. Saving under another name in the app keeps it too; only Save as copy
  mints a new one (`soliddraft_model::Document::new_identity`). The id is not the file name
  and not the part's name.
- `format` is the truth entry's format. Its major version is the number after the slash. A
  reader refuses a major version it does not know.
- `kernel` names the backend whose results the caches hold. Opening never depends on it.
- `sections` lists every entry, or every entry under a folder when the name ends in `/`. A
  reader refuses a file with a required section it does not know, because it would damage
  it. It drops optional sections it does not know, such as a newer build's caches. The
  writer refuses to write an entry that no section covers.
- `references` copies the references the truth holds, so an index can answer "where used"
  from manifests alone.

A part file can also have `settings.json` (optional): viewport quality, export accuracy
and whether to save display data, written only when one differs from its default. It is
outside both hashes, so changing a setting never gives the part a new revision. A reader
that cannot read it opens the part with the default settings. With "save display data"
on (the default), it also has `cache/mesh/coarse.bin` and `cache/mesh/standard.bin`
(optional): its meshes at two display levels. See [tessellation.md](tessellation.md).

The drawing file has `drawing.json` (required), `cache/views/<id>.json` (optional, each
view's line work) and `thumbnail.png` (optional). Entries carry a fixed timestamp, so the
same document gives the same bytes.

`thumbnail.png` is the same optional section in every kind: a small picture a start page
or a file browser can show without opening the document
(`soliddraft_document::thumbnail`). A drawing's is its first sheet, 512 pixels wide. A
part saved from the app gets a 512 by 384 picture from the viewport's own renderer,
drawn into a texture with the part fitted from the default view; a part saved without a
GPU, or from the command line, has none. Thumbnails are outside both hashes.

## Hashes

The semantic hash is the document's revision. It is BLAKE3 over the canonical JSON of the
truth entry without its `format` key: object keys sorted, no whitespace, numbers as
`serde_json` writes them. Caches, thumbnails, the writer and the format tag are not in it,
so migrating a file does not change its revision, and two files with the same design have
the same revision however they were formatted. Several truth entries hash in name order,
each preceded by its name.

The geometry hash leaves out what does not decide the shape. For a part that is the part's
name, each feature's name and `via_assistant` flag, every `label` (the words a
reference keeps for repair prompts), and the material and appearances (`material`,
`appearances` and `snapshots`, see [materials.md](materials.md)). Renaming a feature or
painting a face changes the semantic hash and not the geometry hash.

Neither hash depends on Rust `Debug` output.

## References

```json
{
  "id": "3f0c2a4e-7b1d-4c55-9a0e-2d6f8e1b9c47",
  "kind": "part",
  "path": "../parts/bracket.dwprt",
  "pinned": "blake3:...",
  "configuration": "c-long",
  "display_state": "exploded",
  "locator": "..."
}
```

- `id` is what the target must be. A reference without an id is unbound: it was migrated
  from a drawing that recorded none, or it points at a test recipe, which has none. It
  resolves by its path only and is bound the first time it resolves to a document.
- `path` is relative to the referencing file's folder, with forward slashes.
- `pinned` is the target's semantic hash when the referencing document was last rebuilt
  against it. The referencing document shows that revision until a Rebuild.
- `configuration` and `display_state` are reserved and left out when empty. Phase 0 writes
  neither and keeps any value it reads. A configuration is a named set of overrides on a
  part or assembly; a display state (visibility, colours, an exploded pose) is a separate
  mechanism, so a colour change never invalidates geometry.
- `locator` is reserved for a revision store's own address of the pinned revision, such as
  a Git commit.

A drawing's `model` is a reference. Phase 2 turns it into a list (`models`), one per part
or assembly on the sheet.

## Finding a reference's target

`Resolver::resolve` tries, in order:

1. a document open in this session with the reference's id, because an edited, unsaved part
   must win over its file;
2. the stored path, accepted only when the file there has the reference's id and kind. When
   the stored path has an old extension, the file beside it under the current one comes
   first if it has the same id: it is the same document, saved since;
3. the folder index: the referencing file's folder and its subfolders, then the
   referenced-documents folders from File locations. This finds renamed and moved files.
   When copies share the id, the one at the pinned revision wins, then the nearest;
4. otherwise the reference is missing.

A file with the right name and another id is never taken. It shows up as a repair
candidate. Resolving never rewrites the stored path: a target found elsewhere reports its
new relative path (`Target::new_path`), and the referencing document stores it when it is

name first.

`resolve::repair` points a reference at a file the user picked. The file must have the
reference's kind, and the same id unless the user asked to replace the document. The
pinned revision stays, so the drawing goes on showing what it showed until a Rebuild.
`resolve::repin` is what a Rebuild does to each reference: rebind, then pin at the target's
current revision.

## Pinned revisions and Rebuild

A drawing opens showing the part revision it is pinned at: its views' line work is cached
in the file and was made from that revision. An edited part changes nothing in the drawing
until a Rebuild (`soliddraft draw --update`, `soliddraft doc rebuild`, Update views in the
app) regenerates the views, re-resolves the annotations and re-pins the reference. While
the part and the drawing are both open in the app, automatic update still follows each
rebuild of that part, as before.

Exact work on a pinned revision that is not current (measuring it, projecting a new view
of it) needs that revision's bytes. They come from a `RevisionStore`:

```rust
pub trait RevisionStore: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn fetch(&self, id: DocumentId, revision: &ContentHash) -> Result<Vec<u8>, StoreError>;
    fn record(&self, id: DocumentId, revision: &ContentHash, bytes: &[u8]);
}
```

Phase 0 has `CacheOnlyStore`: the revisions this session opened or saved, nothing older.
When it does not have one, the error says to Rebuild. A Git store (desktop only) comes
next, and a SolidDraft PDM later; the screens stay the same whichever store is behind them.

## Saving

Every document writer, the drawing exports and the settings file go through
`save_atomic`: the bytes go to a hidden temporary file in the target's folder, are flushed,
and the temporary file is renamed over the target. A failed save leaves the previous file
whole.

## Backups

Saving from the app keeps the previous version of the file when the new bytes differ
(`soliddraft_document::Backups`). Backup 1 is the newest; older ones move up a number and
those past the count are deleted. Saving unchanged bytes keeps the backups as they are.
Backups sit beside the document as `bracket.dwprt.1.bak`, or in a backup folder as
`bracket.dwprt.<folder tag>.1.bak`, where the tag tells apart documents with the same
name in different folders. The `.bak` ending keeps a backup out of the folder index, so a
reference never resolves to one. A backup that cannot be made does not stop the save;
the status bar says so.

## Autosave and recovery

While a part or drawing has unsaved changes, autosave writes a recovery copy of it into
this run's session folder, `recovery/session-<pid>-<time>/` in the config directory. A
copy is due when the interval has passed since the first unsaved edit, or sooner after
the set number of edits (`soliddraft_document::autosave`). The interface captures an
immutable snapshot of the document data. A writer thread hashes, serializes and writes
it without display meshes or the drawing's thumbnail. A part snapshot holds no kernel
bodies, build cache or undo history. The copy is written atomically and never touches
the user's file.
Saving a document, or replacing it with New or Open, deletes its copy; quitting deletes
the session folder.

A recovery copy, `<id>.dwprt.recovery` or `<id>.dwdrw.recovery`, is a zip of
`recovery.json` (`soliddraft-recovery/1`: id, kind, name, the file's path, when it was
written, its revision) and `document`, the document file's bytes.

Each running app holds a lock on its session folder's `session.lock`. At start, a session
folder whose lock is free belonged to an app that ended without quitting. Its copies are
offered for restore when the document was never saved, its file is gone or unreadable,
or the file has another revision and was saved before the copy was written. Copies whose
work the file already holds are deleted. Damaged copies are reported once and moved to
`recovery/damaged/`. A restored document opens with unsaved changes at its old path, and
its copy stays protected until it is saved. Offers left undecided stay for the next
start.

The settings file holds the policy under `documents`:

```json
{
  "documents": {
    "autosave": { "enabled": true, "interval_seconds": 120, "edits": 10 },
    "recovery_folder": "/fast/disk/soliddraft-recovery",
    "backups": { "count": 1, "folder": "/backups/soliddraft" }
  }
}
```

Every key is optional. `edits: 0` waits for the interval only, and `count: 0` keeps no
backups. The browser build has no autosave or backups: its files are downloads.

# Documents and references

Parts, assemblies and drawings are separate files. A drawing or an assembly
references the parts it shows, by id. This page is the schema of those files and the rules
for following a reference. The code is `crates/soliddraft-document`; the part and drawing
crates write their files through it.

## Kinds and file names

| Kind | Saved as | Also opens | Truth entry | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Part | `.dwprt` | `.dwpart` | `part.json` | `soliddraft-part/2` |
| Assembly | `.dwasm` | | `assembly.json` | `soliddraft-assembly/1` |
| Drawing | `.dwdrw` | `.dwdrawing` | `drawing.json` | `soliddraft-drawing/2` |

A file under an old extension opens, and saving it writes the current name beside it. The
old file stays where it was. Assemblies are described in [assemblies.md](assemblies.md).

Files with `draftwell-document`, `draftwell-part`, `draftwell-assembly` or
`draftwell-drawing` format prefixes still open. Saving writes the SolidDraft prefixes
and keeps the document id and revision. Document settings also accept the earlier
`draftwell-settings/1` tag. The supported major versions have not changed.

## Damaged and newer files

A file that is truncated, is not an archive, has an entry that does not parse or is missing one is refused with an error that says the file is damaged. A file from a newer SolidDraft (a newer envelope, a format major version this build does not read, a required section it does not know) or of another kind is refused with an error that says so. A truth entry with no format tag says that it has none. Nothing that refuses a file writes to it, replaces it or leaves a stray file beside it; the tests are in `crates/soliddraft-cli/tests/damaged_files.rs` (see [ci.md](ci.md)).

## The envelope

Every document file is a zip whose first entry is `manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "envelope": "soliddraft-document/1",
  "id": "3f0c2a4e-7b1d-4c55-9a0e-2d6f8e1b9c47",
  "kind": "part",
  "format": "soliddraft-part/2",
  "writer": "soliddraft 0.1.0",
  "kernel": "smlib c9c5979",
  "semantic_hash": "blake3:...",
  "geometry_hash": "blake3:...",
  "sections": [
    { "name": "part.json", "required": true }
  ],
  "references": []
}
```

- `id` is a random UUID (version 4) minted when the document is created. Renaming or moving
  the file keeps it. Saving under another name in the app keeps it too; only Save as copy
  mints a new one (`soliddraft_model::Document::new_identity`). The id is not the file name
  and not the part's name.
- `format` is the truth entry's format. Its major version is the number after the slash. A
  reader refuses a major version it does not know.
- `kernel` names the backend whose results the caches hold. Opening never depends on it.
- `sections` lists every entry, or every entry under a folder when the name ends in `/`. A
  reader refuses a file with a required section it does not know, because it would damage
  it. It drops optional sections it does not know, such as a newer build's caches. The
  writer refuses to write an entry that no section covers.
- `references` copies the references the truth holds, so an index can answer "where used"
  from manifests alone.

A part file can also have `settings.json` (optional): viewport quality, export accuracy
and whether to save display data, written only when one differs from its default. It is
outside both hashes, so changing a setting never gives the part a new revision. A reader
that cannot read it opens the part with the default settings. With "save display data"
on (the default), it also has `cache/mesh/coarse.bin` and `cache/mesh/standard.bin`
(optional): its meshes at two display levels. See [tessellation.md](tessellation.md).

The drawing file has `drawing.json` (required), `cache/views/<id>.json` (optional, each
view's line work) and `thumbnail.png` (optional). Entries carry a fixed timestamp, so the
same document gives the same bytes.

`thumbnail.png` is the same optional section in every kind: a small picture a start page
or a file browser can show without opening the document
(`soliddraft_document::thumbnail`). A drawing's is its first sheet, 512 pixels wide. A
part saved from the app gets a 512 by 384 picture from the viewport's own renderer,
drawn into a texture with the part fitted from the default view; a part saved without a
GPU, or from the command line, has none. Thumbnails are outside both hashes.

## Hashes

The semantic hash is the document's revision. It is BLAKE3 over the canonical JSON of the
truth entry without its `format` key: object keys sorted, no whitespace, numbers as
`serde_json` writes them. Caches, thumbnails, the writer and the format tag are not in it,
so migrating a file does not change its revision, and two files with the same design have
the same revision however they were formatted. Several truth entries hash in name order,
each preceded by its name.

The geometry hash leaves out what does not decide the shape. For a part that is the part's
name, each feature's name and `via_assistant` flag, every `label` (the words a
reference keeps for repair prompts), and the material and appearances (`material`,
`appearances` and `snapshots`, see [materials.md](materials.md)). Renaming a feature or
painting a face changes the semantic hash and not the geometry hash. The `values`
table is also excluded: bound inputs are stored as resolved feature parameters, and
renaming their expressions changes no shape. Readers check that those parameters
agree with their drivers before accepting the file.

Neither hash depends on Rust `Debug` output.

## References

```json
{
  "id": "3f0c2a4e-7b1d-4c55-9a0e-2d6f8e1b9c47",
  "kind": "part",
  "path": "../parts/bracket.dwprt",
  "pinned": "blake3:...",
  "configuration": "c-long",
  "display_state": "exploded",
  "locator": "..."
}
```

- `id` is what the target must be. A reference without an id is unbound: it was migrated
  from a drawing that recorded none, or it points at a test recipe, which has none. It
  resolves by its path only and is bound the first time it resolves to a document.
- `path` is relative to the referencing file's folder, with forward slashes.
- `pinned` is the target's semantic hash when the referencing document was last rebuilt
  against it. The referencing document shows that revision until a Rebuild.
- `configuration` and `display_state` are reserved and left out when empty. Phase 0 writes
  neither and keeps any value it reads. A configuration is a named set of overrides on a
  part or assembly; a display state (visibility, colours, an exploded pose) is a separate
  mechanism, so a colour change never invalidates geometry.
- `locator` is reserved for a revision store's own address of the pinned revision, such as
  a Git commit.

A drawing's `model` is a reference. Phase 2 turns it into a list (`models`), one per part
or assembly on the sheet.

## Finding a reference's target

`Resolver::resolve` tries, in order:

1. a document open in this session with the reference's id, because an edited, unsaved part
   must win over its file;
2. the stored path, accepted only when the file there has the reference's id and kind. When
   the stored path has an old extension, the file beside it under the current one comes
   first if it has the same id: it is the same document, saved since;
3. the folder index: the referencing file's folder and its subfolders, then the
   referenced-documents folders from File locations. This finds renamed and moved files.
   When copies share the id, the one at the pinned revision wins, then the nearest;
4. otherwise the reference is missing.

candidate. Resolving never rewrites the stored path: a target found elsewhere reports its

reference's kind, and the same id unless the user asked to replace the document. The
pinned revision stays, so the drawing goes on showing what it showed until a Rebuild.

# Modelling (phase 2 plumbing)

Phase 2 makes SolidDraft a parametric modeller: sketches with constraints, extrusions that
add or cut material, fillets and chamfers, persistent references that survive edits,
undo and redo, and a native file. This page covers the crates that do it. The screens on
top of them are described in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Crates

| Crate | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `soliddraft-sketch` | Sketches: points, lines, arcs, circles and construction geometry with relations and dimensions, solved by ezpz behind an app-owned interface, and the closed regions they make. It depends on the kernel interface's profile types only, not on a kernel. |
| `soliddraft-model` | The part document: features, the command layer with undo and redo, rebuild, persistent references, native files. It talks to a kernel only through the `Kernel` trait. |
| `soliddraft-cli` | Adds `soliddraft part [--json] <part.dwprt>...`, which opens part files, rebuilds them and reports every feature's state. |

## Sketches

The sketch model is the one the sketcher was built on, moved into `soliddraft-sketch` so
the model crate stores what the interface edits. Entities own their points: a line has
two, an arc a centre and two ends (counter-clockwise from start to end), a circle a
centre and a radius. Points of different entities are joined by coincident relations,
the SolidWorks and ezpz way, so an entity can be deleted without rewriting its
neighbours. Entity 0 is the origin, a fixed point. Ids are never reused.

| Entities | Relations and dimensions |
|---|---|
| point, line, arc, circle; any of them can be construction geometry | coincident, point on a curve, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal, midpoint, concentric, fixed; aligned, horizontal and vertical distance, point-to-line distance, angle, radius or diameter |

`solve::solve(sketch, drag, analyse)` moves the geometry until the relations hold and
leaves a `SolveStatus` on the sketch: empty, under defined (with the entities that can
still move), fully defined, over defined (with the relations that could not hold), or
failed. It never fails on an inconsistent sketch: it keeps the solver's best compromise
and names the conflicting relations. A dragged point is a low-priority wish, so real
relations win. Shape builders (`rectangle`, `rounded_rectangle`, `circle_at`, `slot`,
`polyline_loop`) add fully defined geometry and return the dimensions a user edits.

The solver is [ezpz](https://github.com/KittyCAD/ezpz) (MIT), pinned to commit
`915882cc731da31042ce494c89b10334ee57837a` (release 0.2.29) since it has no tagged
releases. Only `solve.rs` uses it, and no ezpz type is public, so planegcs or a
home-grown Gauss-Newton solver can replace it. It converges to 1e-11, so solved corners
land within 1e-9. A line and an arc that share an end are tangent through a right angle
between the line and the radius at that end: ezpz's line-to-circle tangency lets a
shared end slide along the circle with almost no change in the residual.

`Sketch::regions` turns the non-construction curves into closed regions: ends join
through coincident relations or within 1e-6, loops nest by containment, outer loops run
counter-clockwise and holes clockwise, and regions and loops are ordered by entity id so
the same sketch always gives the same order. A region becomes a kernel `Profile` on the
sketch's plane, and every profile segment remembers the sketch entity it came from. An
arc traversed against its own direction, such as a concave bite out of an edge, becomes
`Segment::Arc { clockwise: true }`.

## Features

| Feature | Parameters |
|---|---|
| Sketch | a plane (Top, Front or Right, optionally offset, or a planar face of the part by persistent name) and a sketch |
| Extrude | a profile (a sketch, or a built-in rectangle or circle on a reference plane), boss or cut, blind depth or through all, reversed or not |
| Extrude end | blind, through all, up to the next boundary, or up to a face by persistent name |
| Fillet, Chamfer | edges by persistent name, radius or distance |
| Hole | a planar face by persistent name, centres in the face's sketch frame, diameter, blind depth or through, flat or drill-point tip, counterbore or countersink |
| Linear and circular pattern | a direction and spacing, or an axis and angle, and the number of copies; copies the body and unites the copies with it |
| Mirror | a reference plane or a planar face, and whether the original stays |
| Draft | faces by persistent name, a neutral plane (reference plane or planar face), an angle and the pull's sense |

it. Every closed region of the sketch is swept; four circles make four holes. Through all
reaches past the far side of the body's bounding box.

reversed; the tool is never moved off the face, and the kernel's coplanar Boolean rules

a solid feature. Editing or displaying the hole does not request this proof. The
kernel request includes volume, surface area, centre of mass and centroidal
unit-density inertia. The application response exposes volume, area and centroid
as midpoints of the kernel's proven enclosures. A measurement does not alter the
hole's feature definition or history.

`ci/scenarios/drill-point.json` keeps the 118-degree drill-point build and its
diameter/depth edit under the ordinary 20-million-work policy. Its volume checks
request full mass properties only after the changed body has reached the viewport.
The complete requested measurement has its own elapsed time, separate from the
hole click. Both the original and edited case must retain their existing values.

## Commands, undo and redo

Every change is a `Command`: add, insert, edit, set a sketch dimension, rename, delete,
move, suppress, roll back, or a batch of these as one undo entry. The ribbon, the
assistant (phase 3) and scripts all issue the same commands, and commands serialise to
JSON for the assistant and MCP.

`Document::execute` applies a command, records its exact inverse and rebuilds. Undo is a
stack of those inverses over the document, not over kernel state: undoing an add deletes
the feature, and redoing it puts back the same feature with the same id, so later
entries that name it still apply. A refused command changes nothing; a batch that fails
part-way is unwound.

Moves are refused when a feature would come before one it reads. Deleting a feature is
allowed; the features that read it report what broke.

## Rebuild

A command rebuilds from the first feature it changed, and editing a fillet keeps the
bodies above it. Every feature build is also kept by its exact inputs: the feature, the
exact bytes of its definition, the body it starts from and, for an extrusion, the build
of the sketch it sweeps. Floats count by bit pattern and are never rounded. Kernel bodies are
immutable and a body handle is never reused, so the input body stands for everything
that built it. A rebuild asks for the kept build before building, so:

- renaming a feature builds nothing; checks whose messages name another feature run
  again, without the kernel;
- undo, redo, a value put back, unsuppressing and rolling forward reuse the bodies built
  for those inputs;
- the result is the one a full replay of the saved part gives.

The document owns the kept bodies and releases them when it drops a build. It keeps
them within a budget of retained bytes, 256 MiB unless `Document::set_rebuild_budget`
says otherwise, using the kernel's `retained_bytes` estimate for each body. The builds of the
current tree are always kept; beyond the budget the least recently used others go, with
every build that started from a body they held.

`Document::fork` copies a part and shares its kept builds, so the copy builds only what
changes in it. An assistant proposal's dry run uses a fork and keeps its new builds
until Apply or Discard. Apply imports those builds by exact inputs instead of building
the same geometry again. Import translates the fork's local sketch-build versions;
an intervening edit cannot make an unrelated cached sketch match. Undo still records
the actual commands, and a body is released when the last cache holding it lets go.
The application's proposal copy also shares the current display buffers and cached
LOD meshes, so a sketch-only dry run does not convert or pack the solid's mesh again.

Asynchronous consumers use `execute_deferred`, `undo_deferred` and `redo_deferred`
to change definitions through that same command stack without running the kernel.
`is_dirty()` identifies definitions that have not been rebuilt; body and status getters
still describe the preceding rebuild. A worker rebuilds a fork of the pending document.
After rejecting an obsolete application revision, the caller passes its completed fork
to `rebuild_reusing`. Adoption requires the same document and kernel, a completed
source, and bit-exact feature and rollback definitions. It translates the fork's local
build versions and makes those builds live before trimming the cache. No geometry is
evaluated again, even with a zero-byte reuse budget. History, identity, materials and
settings stay on the receiving document.

Export refuses dirty definitions rather than emitting their preceding body. Saving
authored definitions is still possible, but omits display caches while dirty so an old
mesh cannot acquire the pending definition's geometry hash. Deferred transitions and
explicit `rebuild` operations have distinct journal intents; replay preserves the
unbuilt interval and its export refusal.

Tests count the work, not the rebuild. `soliddraft_kernel_api::counting::Counting`,
behind the `counting` feature, wraps a backend and writes down every operation's tag
and every tessellation. The bracket exit test edits the last feature and checks that only it
was built, that a value put back, undo, redo and renames build nothing, and that each
result, save and reopen included, matches a full replay in statuses, face names,
measures, validation and mesh.

Suppressed features and features below the rollback bar pass the body through
unchanged. A feature's state after a rebuild is one of:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Ok` | built |
| `Suppressed`, `RolledBack` | not built, on purpose |
| `RepairNeeded` | a reference did not resolve to exactly one matching entity |
| `Blocked` | an input feature, such as its sketch, needs a repair, failed or is suppressed |
| `Failed` | bad parameters, a missing input, or a kernel error |

Every state but `Ok` passes the body through, so the rest of the tree still builds.

## Persistent references

A feature never stores a kernel id. It names a face by origin: the feature that
generated it, the generator (start cap, end cap, the side swept from sketch entity 5,
the blend of the feature's edge 2) and an ordinal among that feature's faces with the
same generator, ranked by the sketch region that made them. An edge is named by the two
faces it separates.

The origin is the identity. Catallax records on every face the operations that made it
and the part each one played (its role), and keeps them through later operations: every
piece of a split face keeps the origin, and a face merged from coplanar faces carries
all of their origins. The kernel interface reports them as `FaceInfo::origins`, with the
document's operation tags. On every rebuild each feature says which origin each of its
names stands for, and a name resolves to the faces of the input body that carry that
origin. Renames, splits, merges and dimension edits keep a reference without following
history or comparing geometry. No face role is guessed: a face whose role the interface
cannot express has no name.

- a sketch plane needs one plane, so it accepts the pieces of a split face when they lie
  in one plane;
- an appearance follows every piece;
- a drawing anchor or a fillet edge needs exactly one face or edge.

surface or curve type must not change, and a planar face must still face the same way.

offered when a reference breaks.

its feature with `RepairNeeded`: which reference broke, why (`Missing`, `Ambiguous`,

the nearest face or guesses an identity from geometry. A repair is an ordinary edit with
a new reference.

face for people, such as "Boss-Extrude1 · End cap".

the boss diameter, renames features and the Top datum, splits the plate's top with a
groove, merges it with a flush tab, suppresses and restores the groove, undoes and redoes,
and saves and reopens the part. Every reference survives these steps. Deleting the boss
then raises the repair prompt for the bore's missing plane instead of choosing another.

`datum_names`. Files without labels use Top, Front and Right. Labels affect the semantic
hash, not the geometry hash.

## Native files

A part file (`.dwprt`) is a zip archive with two entries:

- `manifest.json`: the part's id, kind and format, the application and kernel backend
  that saved it, its semantic and geometry hashes and its sections (see
  [documents.md](documents.md)).

repeated ids or a feature that reads one below it. Saving writes next to the target and
renames over it. Part files from before the manifest (`.dwpart`, `recipe.json` with

Application file, byte-upload/recovery and MCP loaders can seed the new document's
existing build cache from the current model. Reuse requires the same document id and
kernel instance, preserves the source's retention budget, and still runs the ordinary
rebuild checks against the incoming definitions. Authored input is journaled before
kernel work; imported builds become live before trimming, so a zero-byte retention
budget does not discard the current tree during handoff. The new cache shares ownership
of retained bodies, not the source's history or built statuses. Changed inputs invalidate
their dependent builds; names and refusals are resolved by the new rebuild.
`Document::from_bytes` and `Document::open` remain cold constructors for fresh replay.


## Exit test

`crates/soliddraft-model/tests/exit_test.rs` builds the sample L-bracket through the command layer, saves and reopens it, edits its base thickness and checks undo, redo and reference repair. Its saved inside fillet builds through Catallax's elementary fillet strips. Supported downstream features keep building.

The document tests also reopen a part containing a chamfer and check that it rebuilds to the same body. Ribbon tests check that waiting commands stay visible, stay disabled and name their stages, and that the switched-on commands are enabled. These run in the workspace CI suite. The application scenarios in `ci/scenarios` build and edit each switched-on feature through MCP.

## Terminal cubic lattice

With a finished body, choose Lattice on the Features ribbon. Cell size and density are in millimetres; density is the constant beam radius. The cubic grid uses the part's origin and axes. Accuracy and minimum detail control certified STL export. The viewport and tree label the displayed mesh as an unproved preview.

The lattice stays last. Edit an earlier feature to rebuild it, or return before the lattice to continue CAD work without losing its settings. The `lattice` and `edit_lattice` agent verbs use the same document commands. Old two-setting lattice files open with their earlier body visible and a message naming the missing cell size and density. Configure those inputs to build the field.

- a drawing anchor or a fillet edge needs exactly one face or edge.

The result is checked against a fingerprint taken when the reference was made: the
surface or curve type must not change, and a planar face must still face the same way.
The fingerprint never chooses a face. Its position and size only rank the candidates
offered when a reference breaks.

A reference that resolves to no entity, to several, or to one that fails the check stops
its feature with `RepairNeeded`: which reference broke, why (`Missing`, `Ambiguous`,
`Mismatch`), and candidates ranked by fingerprint. It never re-attaches silently, picks
the nearest face or guesses an identity from geometry. A repair is an ordinary edit with
a new reference.

`Document::face_ref` and `Document::edge_ref` make a reference from a picked kernel id,
and check that it resolves back to that entity. `Document::plane_ref` makes a sketch
plane reference and also accepts a piece of a split face. `Document::face_label` names a
face for people, such as "Boss-Extrude1 · End cap".

`tests/references.rs` checks survival on the bracket. It edits the plate thickness and
the boss diameter, renames features and the Top datum, splits the plate's top with a
groove, merges it with a flush tab, suppresses and restores the groove, undoes and redoes,
and saves and reopens the part. Every reference survives these steps. Deleting the boss
then raises the repair prompt for the bore's missing plane instead of choosing another.
The same steps run through MCP as the `references` application scenario
([application-loop.md](application-loop.md)).

Datum references store `DatumPlane`, never its display name. `RenameDatumPlane` changes
the label without rebuilding geometry; it is undoable and saved in `part.json` as
`datum_names`. Files without labels use Top, Front and Right. Labels affect the semantic
hash, not the geometry hash.

## Native files

A part file (`.dwprt`) is a zip archive with two entries:

- `manifest.json`: the part's id, kind and format, the application and kernel backend
  that saved it, its semantic and geometry hashes and its sections (see
  [documents.md](documents.md)).
- `part.json`: format tag `soliddraft-part/2`, name, units, every feature with its
  parameters, sketch and references, the rollback bar and the next feature id. No
  kernel ids, no computed geometry: it rebuilds on Catallax.

Writing is deterministic and floats round-trip bit for bit, so saving an opened file
gives the same bytes. A file with a newer major version is refused, as is a recipe with
repeated ids or a feature that reads one below it. Saving writes next to the target and
renames over it. Part files from before the manifest (`.dwpart`, `recipe.json` with
`soliddraft-part/1`) still open, with an id derived from their content.

Application file, byte-upload/recovery and MCP loaders can seed the new document's
existing build cache from the current model. Reuse requires the same document id and
kernel instance, preserves the source's retention budget, and still runs the ordinary
rebuild checks against the incoming definitions. Authored input is journaled before
kernel work; imported builds become live before trimming, so a zero-byte retention
budget does not discard the current tree during handoff. The new cache shares ownership
of retained bodies, not the source's history or built statuses. Changed inputs invalidate
their dependent builds; names and refusals are resolved by the new rebuild.
`Document::from_bytes` and `Document::open` remain cold constructors for fresh replay.


## Exit test

`crates/soliddraft-model/tests/exit_test.rs` builds the sample L-bracket through the command layer, saves and reopens it, edits its base thickness and checks undo, redo and reference repair. Its saved inside fillet builds through Catallax's elementary fillet strips. Supported downstream features keep building.

The document tests also reopen a part containing a chamfer and check that it rebuilds to the same body. Ribbon tests check that waiting commands stay visible, stay disabled and name their stages, and that the switched-on commands are enabled. These run in the workspace CI suite. The application scenarios in `ci/scenarios` build and edit each switched-on feature through MCP.

## Terminal cubic lattice

With a finished body, choose Lattice on the Features ribbon. Cell size and density are in millimetres; density is the constant beam radius. The cubic grid uses the part's origin and axes. Accuracy and minimum detail control certified STL export. The viewport and tree label the displayed mesh as an unproved preview.

The lattice stays last. Edit an earlier feature to rebuild it, or return before the lattice to continue CAD work without losing its settings. The `lattice` and `edit_lattice` agent verbs use the same document commands. Old two-setting lattice files open with their earlier body visible and a message naming the missing cell size and density. Configure those inputs to build the field.

## Named values

The `set_value` tool creates or changes a named expression. `drive` binds a sketch
dimension, numbered from 1, or an extrusion's depth to that expression. For example,
`plate_w = 140` can drive Sketch1 dimension 1 and `plate_w / 2` can drive a depth.
`rename_value` preserves references and updates their displayed text.

Values and bindings persist in the part and participate in undo. A value edit resolves
all its dependents before committing. A cycle, unknown unit or incompatible driver
unit leaves the accepted document unchanged. Change a driven input through its value.

Bare literals use millimetres; bare factors in multiplication and division are scalars.
Length literals support mm, cm, m and in, with exact decimal conversion before rounding
to the stored number. A plain `6 in` is stored as `152.4 mm`. Angle literals use deg.
Expressions with names or operators keep their text. Names are ASCII identifiers,
excluding unit symbols. This increment supports 256 values, dependency depth 32 and 64 tokens per expression.
Automatic dotted names, functions and configuration overrides remain for later slices.

"""Checks must fail closed when evidence or comparison fields are missing."""

import argparse
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import os
import pathlib
import struct
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest import mock

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("scenarios", pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name("run-scenarios.py"))
scenarios = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(scenarios)


class Checks(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_numeric_check_and_missing_evidence(self):
        rule = {"pointer": "/body/volume", "approx": 12000, "tolerance": 0.01}
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.check({"body": {"volume": 12000.005}}, rule)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.check({"body": {"volume": 11999}}, rule)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.check({"body": {}}, rule)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.check({"body": {"volume": None}}, rule)["pass"])

    def test_invalid_or_ambiguous_comparisons_fail(self):
        for rule in ({"pointer": ""}, {"pointer": "", "equals": 3, "minimum": 1},
                     {"pointer": "bad", "equals": 3}):
            self.assertFalse(scenarios.check(3, rule)["pass"])

    def test_expected_repairs_and_the_features_waiting_for_them(self):
        features = [{"name": "Sketch4", "status": "needs repair: Boss · End cap no longer resolves"},
            {"name": "Cut-Extrude1", "status": "error: Sketch4 needs repair first"}, {"name": "Plate", "status": "ok"}]
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.rebuilds(features, ["Sketch4"])["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.rebuilds(features, [])["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.rebuilds(features[2:], ["Sketch4"])["pass"], "an expected prompt is missing")

    def test_references_keep_their_origins(self):
        ref = {"feature_id": "F5", "feature": "Sketch3", "slot": "sketch plane", "origin": "F2 End cap #1",
            "resolved": True, "kernel_origins": [{"tag": "F2.r0.sweep", "role": "end_cap"}], "matches_origin": True}
        known = {}
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.references_kept(known, [ref], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, feature="Boss sketch")], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, origin="F2 Start cap #1")], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, kernel_origins=[{"tag": "F8.r0.sweep"}])], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, matches_origin=False)], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, resolved=False)], [], False)["pass"])
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, resolved=False)], ["Sketch3"], False)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, resolved=True)], ["Sketch3"], False)["pass"])
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.references_kept(known, [dict(ref, resolved=None)], [], False)["pass"], "not built")
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.references_kept(known, [], [], False)["pass"], "a reference vanished")
        known["x"] = "y"
        self.assertTrue(scenarios.references_kept(known, [], [], True)["pass"], "its feature was deleted")

    def test_bundle_paths(self):
        self.assertEqual(scenarios.substitute({"path": "{bundle}/a.dwprt", "n": [1, "{bundle}"]}, "/run"),
            {"path": "/run/a.dwprt", "n": [1, "/run"]})

    def test_timings_list_labelled_steps_only(self):
        steps = [{"tool": "sketch", "pass": True, "timing": {"elapsed_ms": 3.0}},
                 {"tool": "hole", "label": "hole build", "pass": True, "timing": {"elapsed_ms": 812.5}}]
        self.assertEqual(scenarios.timings(steps),
                         [{"label": "hole build", "tool": "hole", "elapsed_ms": 812.5, "pass": True}])

    def test_json_pointer_escapes_and_arrays(self):
        self.assertEqual(scenarios.at({"a/b": [{"~": 2}]}, "/a~1b/0/~0"), 2)


class SavedGeometry(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_recipe_hash_equality_and_missing_hash_fail_closed(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
            folders = [pathlib.Path(temp) / name for name in ("before", "after")]
            for folder in folders:
                folder.mkdir()
            for hashes, expected in ((["a" * 64, "a" * 64], True),
                                     (["a" * 64, "b" * 64], False), ([None, None], False)):
                replies = [scenarios.subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0,
                           json.dumps({"geometry_hash": value}), "") for value in hashes]
                with mock.patch.object(scenarios.subprocess, "run", side_effect=replies):
                    result = scenarios.same_geometry("soliddraft", folders[1], folders[0], 5)
                self.assertEqual(result["pass"], expected)

    def test_checked_step_fails_when_opencascade_or_validity_check_fails(self):
        evidence = {"summary": {"body": {"faces": 6}},
                    "measurement": {"volume_mm3": 1000, "area_mm2": 600}}
        report = {"kind": "step", "solids": 1, "faces": 6, "within_tolerance": True}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
            directory = pathlib.Path(temp)
            (directory / "part.step").write_bytes(b"STEP bytes")
            for error in ("ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'OCP'", "FAIL: invalid solid"):
                replies = [scenarios.subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0, json.dumps({"report": report}), ""),
                           scenarios.subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 1, "", error)]
                with mock.patch.object(scenarios.subprocess, "run", side_effect=replies) as run:
                    checks = scenarios.checked_step_export("soliddraft", "saved.dwprt", directory, evidence, 5)
                self.assertFalse(all(c["pass"] for c in checks))
                self.assertEqual(checks[-1]["check"], "check-step")
                self.assertEqual((directory / "check-step.stderr").read_text(), error)
                self.assertEqual(run.call_args_list[0].args[0][1:3], ["export", "saved.dwprt"])
                self.assertEqual(json.loads((directory / "step-report.json").read_text()), {
                    "report": report, "body": {"faces": 6, "volume": 1000, "area": 600}})


class Latency(unittest.TestCase):
    @staticmethod
    def call(name, elapsed, operations=(), *, nested=False, refused=False, work=None, foreground=True):
        return {"operation": name, "wall_ms": elapsed, "nested": nested, "on_capture_thread": foreground,
                "status": "refused" if refused else "answered", "work": work,
                "operation_log": {"format": "catallax-operation-log/1", "operations": list(operations)}}

    @staticmethod
    def operation(name, elapsed, work=1):
        return {"operation": name, "wall_ms": elapsed, "work": {"used": work}}

    @staticmethod
    def segment(elapsed, calls=(), **extra):

        ])])
        self.assertFalse(result["pass"])

        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["edit"], 1100)
        self.assertEqual(sum(result["split_ms"].values()), 1100)
        self.assertEqual(result["work"]["edit"], 25)
        self.assertEqual(result["background"]["call_ms"]["display"], 3000)
        self.assertEqual(result["background"]["work"]["display"], 15)

    def test_refusal_keeps_its_whole_wait_and_work(self):

        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["refusal"], 600)
        self.assertEqual(result["work"]["refusal"], 7)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["display"], 0)

    def test_drawing_reconstruction_is_not_hidden_as_rendering(self):
        result = scenarios.timing("rollback", [self.segment(400, [
            self.call("extrude", 200),
            self.call("view_curves", 100),
        ], phase="construction", overhead_phase="display")])
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["construction"], 200)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["display"], 200)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["edit"], 0)

    def test_exact_budget_boundary_and_one_microsecond_over(self):
        for tool, limit in (("box", 100), ("boolean", 500), ("edit_extrude", 1000), ("compare", 2000)):
            with self.subTest(tool=tool):
                self.assertTrue(scenarios.timing(tool, [self.segment(limit)])["pass"])
                self.assertFalse(scenarios.timing(tool, [self.segment(limit + 0.001)])["pass"])

    def test_invalid_or_overlapping_evidence_fails_closed(self):
        for elapsed in (None, True, -1, float("nan"), float("inf")):
            with self.subTest(elapsed=elapsed), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(elapsed)])
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [{"source": "missing", "elapsed_ms": 1}])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(10, [self.call("extrude", 11)])])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(10, [
                self.call("extrude", 5, [self.operation("mesh", 6)]),
            ])])
        call = self.call("extrude", 1)

        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):

class KnownBudgets(unittest.TestCase):
    known = {("bracket", 6): {"scenario": "bracket", "step": 6, "tool": "extrude",
                            "last_measured_ms": 2000}}

    def verdict(self, elapsed, scenario="bracket", number=6, tool="extrude"):
        latency = scenarios.timing(tool, [Latency.segment(elapsed)])
        return scenarios.accept_latency(scenario, number, tool, latency, self.known)

    def test_approved_overrun_is_accepted_only_for_its_exact_step_and_tool(self):
        accepted = self.verdict(2240)
        self.assertTrue(accepted["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(accepted["within_budget"])
        self.assertEqual(accepted["status"], "known-over-budget")
        self.assertFalse(self.verdict(2240, scenario="another-bracket")["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(self.verdict(2240, number=7)["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(self.verdict(2240, tool="cut")["pass"])

    def test_listed_step_still_fails_above_20_percent_regression(self):
        boundary = self.verdict(2400)
        self.assertTrue(boundary["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(boundary["within_budget"])
        self.assertEqual(boundary["budget_ms"], 1000)
        over = self.verdict(2400.001)
        self.assertFalse(over["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(over["within_budget"])
        self.assertEqual(over["status"], "known-gap-regression")
        self.assertEqual(over["budget_ms"], 1000)

    def test_listed_step_can_improve_without_changing_the_strict_budget(self):
        for elapsed in (999.999, 1000):
            with self.subTest(elapsed=elapsed):
                improved = self.verdict(elapsed)
                self.assertTrue(improved["pass"])
                self.assertTrue(improved["within_budget"])
                self.assertEqual(improved["status"], "pass")

    def test_unlisted_step_keeps_its_strict_budget_boundary(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.verdict(1000, number=7)["pass"])
        over = self.verdict(1000.001, number=7)
        self.assertFalse(over["pass"])
        self.assertEqual(over["status"], "over-budget")

class RunnerEndToEnd(unittest.TestCase):
    """The real run() against a synthetic MCP server, so the click ends where a user sees it."""

    def run_step(self, mode, measure=False, timeout=5, strict=False, known=None, extra=None):
        step = {"tool": "extrude", "arguments": {}}
        step.update(extra or {})
        if measure:
            step["checks"] = [{"pointer": "/measurement/volume_mm3", "approx": 1.0}]
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = pathlib.Path(directory)
            scenario = root / "scenario.json"
            scenario.write_text(json.dumps({"format": "soliddraft-scenario/1", "name": "synthetic-gate",
                                            "steps": [step]}))
            args = argparse.Namespace(scenario=scenario, out=root / "run", soliddraft=str(FAKE),
                                      catallax_verify="unused", timeout=timeout, strict=strict)
            os.environ["FAKE_MODE"] = mode
            os.environ["FAKE_PIN"] = scenarios.pinned_revision()
            try:
                with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), \
                        mock.patch.object(scenarios, "load_known_over_budget", return_value=known or {}):
                    code = scenarios.run(args)
            finally:
                del os.environ["FAKE_MODE"], os.environ["FAKE_PIN"]
            report = json.loads((args.out / "result.json").read_text())
        checks = {c["check"]: c for c in (report["steps"][0]["checks"] if report["steps"] else [])
                  if isinstance(c["check"], str)}
        self.code = code
        return report, checks

        for mode, declared, expected in [("field-view", True, True), ("field-view", False, False),

            with self.subTest(mode=mode, declared=declared):

class Latency(unittest.TestCase):
    @staticmethod
    def call(name, elapsed, operations=(), *, nested=False, refused=False, work=None, foreground=True):
        return {"operation": name, "wall_ms": elapsed, "nested": nested, "on_capture_thread": foreground,
                "status": "refused" if refused else "answered", "work": work,
                "operation_log": {"format": "catallax-operation-log/1", "operations": list(operations)}}

    @staticmethod
    def operation(name, elapsed, work=1):
        return {"operation": name, "wall_ms": elapsed, "work": {"used": work}}

    @staticmethod
    def segment(elapsed, calls=(), **extra):
        return {"source": "kernel.json", "elapsed_ms": elapsed, "kernel": {"calls": list(calls)}, **extra}

    def test_display_and_requested_measurement_are_in_the_click_budget(self):
        command = self.segment(400, [
            self.call("extrude", 300, [
                self.operation("extrude", 200, 20),
                self.operation("mesh", 50, 5),
            ], work={"used": 25}),
            self.call("mass_properties", 60, [self.operation("mass_properties", 55, 6)]),
        ])
        result = scenarios.timing("extrude", [command, self.segment(650, phase="display")])
        self.assertFalse(result["pass"])
        self.assertEqual(result["elapsed_ms"], 1050)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"], {
            "construction": 290, "edit": 0, "display": 700, "measurement": 60, "refusal": 0,
        })
        self.assertEqual(result["work"], {
            "construction": 20, "edit": 0, "display": 5, "measurement": 6, "refusal": 0,
        })

    def test_nested_drawing_queries_are_not_charged_twice(self):
        result = scenarios.timing("edit_extrude", [self.segment(200, [
            self.call("tessellate", 70, nested=True),
            self.call("view_curves", 100, [self.operation("mesh", 70, 5)], work={"used": 5}),
        ])])
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["display"], 100)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["edit"], 100)
        self.assertEqual(sum(result["work"].values()), 5)

    def test_concurrent_background_mesh_keeps_external_wait_and_its_work(self):
        result = scenarios.timing("edit_extrude", [self.segment(1100, [
            self.call("tessellate", 3000, [self.operation("mesh", 2900, 15)],
                      work={"used": 15}, foreground=False),
            self.call("tessellate_edges", 500, nested=True, foreground=False),
            self.call("extrude", 500, work={"used": 25}),
        ])])
        self.assertFalse(result["pass"])
        self.assertEqual(result["elapsed_ms"], 1100)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["edit"], 1100)
        self.assertEqual(sum(result["split_ms"].values()), 1100)
        self.assertEqual(result["work"]["edit"], 25)
        self.assertEqual(result["background"]["call_ms"]["display"], 3000)
        self.assertEqual(result["background"]["work"]["display"], 15)

    def test_refusal_keeps_its_whole_wait_and_work(self):
        result = scenarios.timing("cut", [self.segment(600, [
            self.call("boolean", 500, [self.operation("mesh", 50, 3)],
                      refused=True, work={"used": 7}),
        ], phase="refusal")])
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["refusal"], 600)
        self.assertEqual(result["work"]["refusal"], 7)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["display"], 0)

    def test_drawing_reconstruction_is_not_hidden_as_rendering(self):
        result = scenarios.timing("rollback", [self.segment(400, [
            self.call("extrude", 200),
            self.call("view_curves", 100),
        ], phase="construction", overhead_phase="display")])
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["construction"], 200)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["display"], 200)
        self.assertEqual(result["split_ms"]["edit"], 0)

    def test_exact_budget_boundary_and_one_microsecond_over(self):
        for tool, limit in (("box", 100), ("boolean", 500), ("edit_extrude", 1000), ("compare", 2000)):
            with self.subTest(tool=tool):
                self.assertTrue(scenarios.timing(tool, [self.segment(limit)])["pass"])
                self.assertFalse(scenarios.timing(tool, [self.segment(limit + 0.001)])["pass"])

    def test_invalid_or_overlapping_evidence_fails_closed(self):
        for elapsed in (None, True, -1, float("nan"), float("inf")):
            with self.subTest(elapsed=elapsed), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(elapsed)])
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [{"source": "missing", "elapsed_ms": 1}])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(10, [self.call("extrude", 11)])])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(10, [
                self.call("extrude", 5, [self.operation("mesh", 6)]),
            ])])
        call = self.call("extrude", 1)
        del call["on_capture_thread"]
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            scenarios.timing("extrude", [self.segment(10, [call])])

            "selectable not a bool": dict(self.good, selectable=1),
            "no selection count": {"request": 3, "revision": 7},
            "older revision": dict(self.good, revision=6),
            "older request": dict(self.good, request=2),
            "pending": dict(self.good, pending=True),
            "no request": {"revision": 7, "selectable": True},
            "no revision": {"request": 3, "selectable": True},
            "boolean revision": dict(self.good, revision=True),
        }
        for label, reply in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(label):
                self.assertIsNotNone(scenarios.answers(3, self.command, reply, True))
        self.assertIsNotNone(scenarios.answers(3, self.command, None))
        self.assertIsNotNone(scenarios.answers(3, {"request": 3}, self.good), "the command has no revision")

class RunnerEndToEnd(unittest.TestCase):
    """The real run() against a synthetic MCP server, so the click ends where a user sees it."""

    def run_step(self, mode, measure=False, timeout=5, strict=False, known=None, extra=None):
        step = {"tool": "extrude", "arguments": {}}
        step.update(extra or {})
        if measure:
            step["checks"] = [{"pointer": "/measurement/volume_mm3", "approx": 1.0}]
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            root = pathlib.Path(directory)
            scenario = root / "scenario.json"
            scenario.write_text(json.dumps({"format": "soliddraft-scenario/1", "name": "synthetic-gate",
                                            "steps": [step]}))
            args = argparse.Namespace(scenario=scenario, out=root / "run", soliddraft=str(FAKE),
                                      catallax_verify="unused", timeout=timeout, strict=strict)
            os.environ["FAKE_MODE"] = mode
            os.environ["FAKE_PIN"] = scenarios.pinned_revision()
            try:
                with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), \
                        mock.patch.object(scenarios, "load_known_over_budget", return_value=known or {}):
                    code = scenarios.run(args)
            finally:
                del os.environ["FAKE_MODE"], os.environ["FAKE_PIN"]
            report = json.loads((args.out / "result.json").read_text())
        checks = {c["check"]: c for c in (report["steps"][0]["checks"] if report["steps"] else [])
                  if isinstance(c["check"], str)}
        self.code = code
        return report, checks

    def test_only_the_declared_field_view_refusal_is_accepted(self):
        for mode, declared, expected in [("field-view", True, True), ("field-view", False, False),
                                         ("wrong-view-error", True, False), ("ok", True, False)]:
            with self.subTest(mode=mode, declared=declared):
                report, _ = self.run_step(mode, extra={"view": "unavailable"} if declared else {})
                self.assertEqual(report["pass"], expected)

    def test_export_report_checks_and_refusals_run_through_the_cli(self):
        exports = [{"format": "stl", "checks": [{"pointer": "/report/deviation_bound_mm", "maximum": 0.1}]}]
        report, _ = self.run_step("ok", extra={"exports": exports})
        self.assertTrue(report["pass"])
        exports[0]["checks"][0]["maximum"] = 0.01
        report, _ = self.run_step("ok", extra={"exports": exports})
        self.assertFalse(report["pass"])
        for mode, expected in [("export-refused", True), ("export-refused-written", False),
                               ("export-refused-wrong", False), ("ok", False)]:
            report, _ = self.run_step(mode, extra={"exports": [{"format": "step", "refused": "field parts export as meshes"}]})
            self.assertEqual(report["pass"], expected, mode)

    def test_a_visible_selectable_edit_ends_the_click(self):
        report, checks = self.run_step("ok")
        self.assertTrue(checks["click ends at a visible selectable edit"]["pass"])
        interval = report["steps"][0]["intervals"]["preview"]
        self.assertEqual(interval["ends"], "visible selectable edit")
        self.assertEqual(interval["verdict"], "strict-pass")

    def test_a_display_without_its_evidence_fails_the_step(self):
        report, checks = self.run_step("lost-display")
        self.assertFalse(checks["display evidence written"]["pass"])
        self.assertIn("display.json", checks["display evidence written"]["reason"])
        self.assertNotEqual(report["steps"][0]["intervals"]["preview"]["ends"], "command reply, no solid to show")
        self.assertFalse(report["steps"][0]["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(report["pass"])

    def test_a_display_that_reports_no_solid_ends_the_click_at_the_reply(self):
        report, checks = self.run_step("no-solid", strict=True)
        self.assertNotIn("click ends at a visible selectable edit", checks)
        self.assertNotIn("live hidden-line view", checks)
        self.assertEqual(report["steps"][0]["intervals"]["preview"]["ends"], "command reply, no solid to show")
        self.assertTrue(report["pass"])
        self.assertEqual(self.code, 0)

    def test_a_stale_or_failed_no_solid_reply_cannot_skip_the_display(self):
        for mode, reason in (("stale-no-solid", "stale"), ("failed-no-solid", "failed")):
            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
                report, checks = self.run_step(mode)
                self.assertFalse(checks["no-solid reply answers this request"]["pass"])
                self.assertIn(reason, checks["no-solid reply answers this request"]["reason"])
                self.assertNotEqual(report["steps"][0]["intervals"]["preview"]["ends"],
                                    "command reply, no solid to show")
                self.assertFalse(report["pass"])

    def test_early_command_reply_cannot_pass(self):

    def test_stale_measurement_cannot_satisfy_the_request(self):

    def test_oracle_failure_and_report_mismatch_fail_the_export(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            directory = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            args = argparse.Namespace(soliddraft=str(FAKE), timeout=5)
            real_cli = scenarios.cli
            def fake_oracle(binary, arguments, output, label, timeout):
                if label.endswith("-oracle"):
                    data = bytearray((directory / "part.stl").read_bytes())
                    struct.pack_into("<d", data, 68, self.bound)
                    (directory / "part.stl").write_bytes(data)
                    (directory / f"{label}.stdout").write_text(json.dumps({"bound_mm": self.bound}))
                    return {"check": label, "pass": self.oracle_pass}
                return real_cli(binary, arguments, output, label, timeout)
            spec = {"format": "stl", "oracle": {"box": [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], "cell": 5,
                    "radius": 1, "accuracy": "1/10", "euler": 2}}
            for self.oracle_pass, self.bound, expected in [(True, 0.1, True), (False, 0.1, False), (True, 0.2, False)]:
                with mock.patch.object(scenarios, "cli", side_effect=fake_oracle):
                    self.assertEqual(scenarios.export_check(args, directory, spec, {})["pass"], expected)

    def test_oracle_receives_the_caps_the_header_must_record(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            directory = pathlib.Path(tmp)
            args = argparse.Namespace(soliddraft=str(FAKE), timeout=5)
            real_cli, seen = scenarios.cli, []
            def record(binary, arguments, output, label, timeout):
                if label.endswith("-oracle"):
                    seen.append([str(a) for a in arguments])
                    return {"check": label, "pass": True}
                return real_cli(binary, arguments, output, label, timeout)
            oracle = {"box": [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], "cell": 5, "radius": 1, "accuracy": "1/10", "euler": 2}
            for spec_oracle, expected in [(oracle, None), ({**oracle, "caps": [2000000, 1000000]}, ["2000000", "1000000"])]:
                seen.clear()
                with mock.patch.object(scenarios, "cli", side_effect=record):
                    scenarios.export_check(args, directory, {"format": "stl", "oracle": spec_oracle}, {})
                command = seen[0]
                actual = command[command.index("--caps") + 1:command.index("--caps") + 3] if "--caps" in command else None
                self.assertEqual(actual, expected)

class Trends(unittest.TestCase):
    @staticmethod
    def samples(times):
        return [{"number": 3 + 4 * i, "tool": "sketch", "feature_count": 3 + 2 * i,
                 "timing": {"elapsed_ms": elapsed}} for i, elapsed in enumerate(times)]

    def verdict(self, rows):
        return scenarios.trend_checks([{"tool": "sketch", "from_step": 3}], rows)[0]

    def test_growth_fails_even_when_every_step_meets_its_click_budget(self):
        rows = self.samples([100 + 2 * i for i in range(30)])
        self.assertTrue(all(scenarios.timing("sketch", [Latency.segment(row["timing"]["elapsed_ms"])])["pass"]
                            for row in rows))
        result = self.verdict(rows)
        self.assertFalse(result["pass"])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(result["growth_ms"], 58)

    def test_flat_series_tolerates_jitter_and_a_single_stall(self):
        times = [300 + (-8, -2, 3, 7)[i % 4] for i in range(30)]
        times[12] = 900
        self.assertTrue(self.verdict(self.samples(times))["pass"])

    def test_trend_noise_boundary_does_not_change_click_budgets(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.verdict(self.samples([300 + 25 * i / 29 for i in range(30)]))["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(self.verdict(self.samples([300 + 25.1 * i / 29 for i in range(30)]))["pass"])
        self.assertFalse(scenarios.timing("sketch", [Latency.segment(1000.001)])["pass"])

    def test_missing_or_nonincreasing_feature_count_cannot_pass(self):
        for damage in ("missing", "repeated", "missing_time", "truncated"):
            rows = self.samples([300] * 30)
            if damage == "missing":
                del rows[5]["feature_count"]
            elif damage == "repeated":
                rows[5]["feature_count"] = rows[4]["feature_count"]
            elif damage == "missing_time":
                del rows[5]["timing"]
            else:
                rows = rows[:9]
            with self.subTest(damage=damage):
                self.assertFalse(self.verdict(rows)["pass"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

//! Assembly command registry rows.

use super::*;
use crate::assembly::AssemblyAction;
use soliddraft_assistant::tools::schema::string;

const ASSEMBLY: &str = "It works on the assembly open in the window; soliddraft asm makes, places and saves assembly \
                        files without it";

/// Why an assembly command is off in the browser build, whose loader has no threads.
fn desktop_only(_: &AppState) -> Option<String> {
    cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32").then(|| "Assemblies open in the desktop app".to_owned())
}

fn path_params() -> Vec<(&'static str, Value)> {
    vec![("path", string("An assembly file path ending in .dwasm"))]
}

pub(super) fn registry() -> Vec<CommandSpec> {
    use Size::{Large, Small};
    let ctrl = Modifiers::COMMAND;
    let ctrl_shift = Modifiers::COMMAND | Modifiers::SHIFT;
    let cmd = CommandSpec::new;
    vec![
        // Assemblies. `soliddraft asm` does the same to assembly files from the command line.
        cmd("new_assembly", "New assembly", Icon::Tree, "Start a new, empty assembly in a tab beside the part")
            .both()
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::New))
            .when(|_| !cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32"))
            .hint(desktop_only)
            .app_only(ASSEMBLY),
        cmd("make_assembly", "Make assembly", Icon::Tree, "Start an assembly that places this saved part")
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::FromPart))
            .when(|s| has_body(s) && !cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32"))
            .hint(desktop_only)
            .agents(Agents::Mcp, "Places the saved, unmodified part at the origin, floating.", Vec::new)
            .undo(Undo::Step),
        cmd("insert_component", "Insert component", Icon::Import, "Place a part or an assembly file in the assembly")
            .assembly()
            .on(Tab::Assembly, "Component", Large)
            .key(Scope::Assembly, ctrl, Key::I)
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::Insert(None)))
            .app_only(ASSEMBLY),
        cmd("assembly_save", "Save assembly", Icon::Save, "Save the assembly with copies of the parts it shows")
            .assembly()
            .on(Tab::Assembly, "File", Small)
            .key(Scope::Assembly, ctrl, Key::S)
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::Save(None)))
            .agents(Agents::Mcp, "Saves the assembly and its accepted display copies.", path_params),
        cmd("assembly_save_as", "Save assembly as", Icon::Save, "Save the assembly under a new name")
            .assembly()
            .on(Tab::Assembly, "File", Small)
            .key(Scope::Assembly, ctrl_shift, Key::S)
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::SaveAs))
            .app_only(ASSEMBLY),
        cmd("show_assembly", "Show assembly", Icon::Tree, "Switch to the open assembly")
            .both()
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::Show))
            .when(|s| s.assembly.session.is_some())
            .agents(Agents::Mcp, "Makes the assembly active.", Vec::new),
        cmd("assembly_show_part", "Show part", Icon::Extrude, "Switch to the open part")
            .assembly()
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::ShowPart))
            .agents(Agents::Mcp, "Makes the part active.", Vec::new),
        cmd("assembly_update", "Update", Icon::Tree, "Accept the current revisions of every source together")
            .assembly()
            .on(Tab::Assembly, "Component", Large)
            .run(|_| AppAction::Assembly(AssemblyAction::Update))
            .agents(Agents::Mcp, "Keeps all accepted revisions if any source is missing or cannot be shown.", Vec::new)
            .undo(Undo::Step),
    ]
}
